speaker: The Wanderer
current_text: ...Cold. Leaves in my mouth. Great start.

speaker: The Wanderer
current_text: I reach for my name. Nothing. Not even the shape of one.

speaker: The Wanderer
current_text: Two hands, one of them shaking. I'll start with the other one. ...And I'm not alone.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You wake in a forest clearing with leaves in your hair.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A faint glow of four colors fades from your hand, like a thought you almost had.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Beside you kneels someone hooded, very still, as if they have waited a long time.

speaker: The Rescuer
current_text: Easy. Stay down. Hands like ice, pulse like a rabbit's. We'll fix that later.

speaker: The Rescuer
current_text: Keep your voice low. We are not the only ones in these woods tonight.

speaker: The Wanderer
current_text: I don't know this place. I don't know my own name. ...Who are you?

speaker: The Rescuer
current_text: A friend. That's all I can give you, and it's already more than is safe.

speaker: The Rescuer
current_text: Can you still fight? Still draw on the Paths? Hold out your hand. You always used to... Never mind. Your hand.
new_text: Can you still fight, still draw on the Paths? Hold out your hand like you used to... never mind, just your hand.
writer_note: Tightens the urgent instructions; retains the guarded slip that she knew him before.

speaker: The Wanderer
current_text: ...I feel them. All four, faintly. Like voices through a wall.

speaker: The Rescuer
current_text: Faint will do. It has to. There are torches on the ridge, and they aren't out for a stroll.
new_text: Faint will do - it has to. Those torches on the ridge are looking for us.
writer_note: Keeps the pursuit immediate; removes the stroll aside from the escape beat.

speaker: The Rescuer
current_text: Tell me: which Path resonates the strongest within you?
writer_note: Plain, urgent Path-choice prompt; does not imply he can feel only one Path.

speaker: The Rescuer
current_text: That one, then. Hold on to it, and it will hold on to you.

speaker: The Rescuer
current_text: Behind me is the Forgotten Cave. Follow it all the way through to {town}. Someone there will be waiting for you.

speaker: The Rescuer
current_text: Hear that? They're close. I'll draw them off the other way. They know my face; let them chase it.

speaker: The Rescuer
current_text: So you go on alone. Don't thank me. Thank me when you're somewhere with a roof. Go!

speaker: The Wanderer
current_text: ...Gone, toward the torches. I never even asked their name.

speaker: The Wanderer
current_text: The trees close up that way. The cave, then.

speaker: The Wanderer
current_text: No point getting lost twice in one day. Back to the cave.

speaker: The Wanderer
current_text: Whatever is waiting for me, it's through that cave.

speaker: The Wanderer
current_text: Torches that way. Cave this way. Even with no memory, I can solve this one.
new_text: Torches that way, cave this way. I'll take the one that isn't looking for me.
writer_note: Dry self-preservation; the cave remains the clear direction.

speaker: Foreman Gus
current_text: Foreman Gus. I run the wheels. I keep the grid humming and the hamsters... the *volunteers*... fed. Pre-workout's in the water. Hasn't hit me yet.
new_text: Foreman Gus: wheels turning, grid humming, hamsters... *volunteers*... fed. Pre-workout's in the water, but so far I'm only feeling the water.
writer_note: Keeps all three voice tics; tired anticlimax rather than a hype-man delivery.

speaker: Foreman Gus
current_text: The regime wants a hundred and ten percent. The wheels go to a hundred. The extra ten is me, crying quietly.

speaker: Foreman Gus
current_text: They want the same out of the city wheels up in the Capital. Those crews get told it's cardio. It isn't.

speaker: Foreman Gus
current_text: Is the grid humming? Should be humming. If it's quiet, somebody's resting, and the regime writes that down.
new_text: Grid still humming? If it goes quiet, somebody's resting, and the regime writes that down as a personal insult.
writer_note: Preserves recorded rest and surveillance; the joke targets management.

speaker: Foreman Gus
current_text: You. Fresh legs. The lights are flickering: the regime pipes every watt up to the House of Gains. Somebody should run the Colossal Hamster Wheel up the hill. For us. Wouldn't that be a shame.
new_text: Lights flicker while the regime pipes every watt to the House of Gains. Run the Colossal Hamster Wheel up the hill for us - a little resistance.
writer_note: Electrical resistance / quiet sedition: one pun; keeps the power diversion, place and action explicit.

speaker: Foreman Gus
current_text: Then buy a shake at the protein stand here in the Station. Grid's low on power, crew's low on morale. Same fix. Run the wheel, buy a shake. Quiet gains. Nobody needs to know.
new_text: Then buy a shake at the protein stand in the Swole Station for crew morale. Quiet gains - the revolution comes with a straw.
writer_note: Keeps the second objective and its purpose; small-scale rebellion in the shake image.

speaker: Foreman Gus
current_text: The big wheel up the hill, then a shake from the protein stand. Quiet gains. Tell me when you're done.
new_text: Run the Colossal Hamster Wheel up the hill, then buy a shake at the protein stand in the Swole Station. Quiet gains - tell me when you're done.
writer_note: Names both actions and locations so the reminder stands alone; retains Quiet gains.

speaker: Foreman Gus
current_text: Lights are back on. The grid's HUMMING. ...Sorry. Haven't raised my voice in years. You've earned this.
new_text: The Swole Station's lights are back on, and the grid's HUMMING. Take your reward before I turn this into a pep talk.
writer_note: Keeps restored power, the rare raised voice and the reward; foreman catches himself becoming a coach.

speaker: Foreman Gus
current_text: Don't let the hamsters hear you call them 'volunteers'. They're sensitive.

speaker: Foreman Gus
current_text: The grid's running smooth, and some of it's even staying here. I'd hug you, but I'm a foreman. We nod. ...That was a big nod.

speaker: Foreman Gus
current_text: Foreman Gus. Still on the wheels. Listen to that.

speaker: Foreman Gus
current_text: The grid's at a hundred percent. A HUNDRED. Nobody asking for ten more.
new_text: The grid's at a hundred percent, and nobody wants ten more. Turns out a hundred was all of it.
writer_note: Pays off the unchanged 110-percent setup with exhausted arithmetic.

speaker: Foreman Gus
current_text: I might cry. Into the wheel. For energy.
new_text: I might cry into the wheel for energy. Voluntarily, for once.
writer_note: Retains the tears-for-power joke and pays off the volunteers euphemism as actual choice.

speaker: Foreman Gus
current_text: The wheels turn when they feel like it, and somehow we've never had more power. I'd tell the regime, but there isn't one.

speaker: Basil
current_text: You came back. Good. A Gourmand never stops stirring. I'm stirring nervously, but it counts.
new_text: You came back... good, good. A Gourmand never stops stirring, so technically this panic is a cooking method.
writer_note: Nervous repetition; preserves constant stirring and turns anxiety into kitchen technique.

speaker: Basil
current_text: What do we say? Yes, Chef. Quietly.
new_text: What do we say? "Yes, Chef" - on the lowest possible heat.
writer_note: Kitchen metaphor for the whispered answer; does not steal another speaker's catchphrase.

speaker: Basil
current_text: The Grand Chef has very good hearing, for someone who never tastes a thing.

speaker: Basil
current_text: The real Chef baked a birthday cake for the little prince once. Four layers, one for each Path. He licked the frosting off all four and left the rest.

speaker: Basil
current_text: Chef laughed for a week. Last month I mentioned that cake to her, and she didn't remember it. Chef remembers every cake she's ever baked.

speaker: Basil
current_text: The Special Sauce is down the drain and the golems guard plates again. Yes, Chef!
new_text: The Special Sauce is down the drain and the golems guard plates again. Yes, Chef - finally an order I can stomach!
writer_note: One stomach pun; preserves both liberation facts and the willing Yes, Chef payoff.

speaker: Basil
current_text: Take seconds. You've earned seconds. You've earned thirds. Listen to me, I'm not even whispering.

speaker: The Doppelganger
current_text: Welcome to the Executive Test Kitchen, taster. Ten years in this face and this apron, and not one Gourmand looked twice.

speaker: The Doppelganger
current_text: They never looked at their Chef. They looked at the food.

speaker: The Wanderer
current_text: You never taste your own soup, do you?

speaker: The Doppelganger
current_text: ...Tasting is inefficient. The orders from {capital} asked for golems, not flavour, and the Special Sauce delivers golems.

speaker: The Doppelganger
current_text: "Delicious." That is the word I was given for it. I say it often. I do not know what it means.

speaker: The Doppelganger
current_text: Fine. If you must see. I never liked this chin.
new_text: Then look. I have worn this face long enough.
writer_note: Removes the chin punchline; keeps the unmasking cue and leads into the forgotten-face confession.

speaker: The Doppelganger
current_text: This is what was under it. I wore her face so long that I forgot my own. There is nothing in here to taste with.

speaker: The Doppelganger
current_text: Sit down, taster. I was told to serve you.
